examples.en: Today my husband and I watched a movie, just the two of us.
It's the first time the two of us have traveled alone.
Only my sibling and I, just the two of us, were left in the room.
It's an important matter, so I asked to meet one on one.
Being alone together, just the two of us, feels a bit awkward.
There's too much food for just the two of us.

explain: '둘이'보다 다른 사람 없이 오직 두 사람뿐이라는 느낌이 강해요. 주로 '단둘이(서)'처럼 붙여 쓰고, 따로 이야기하거나 데이트할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It stresses that there is nobody else, more than plain '둘이'. It is mostly used as '단둘이(서)', and suits private talks or dates.

examples.en: I went on a picnic with my classmates.
A classmate helped me with my homework.
Among my classmates there are also foreigners.
I asked a classmate about a problem I did not know.
I keep in touch with a classmate after graduation.

examples.ko: 그 애는 동급생인데도 저보다 한 살 많아요.
examples.en: That kid is in my grade but one year older than me.

explain: 같은 학년 친구는 '동급생'이고, 나이가 같은 친구는 '동갑'이에요. 그래서 동급생이어도 나이가 다를 수 있어요. 학년이 다르면 '선배', '후배'라고 불러요.
explain_en: A friend in the same grade is a '동급생', while a friend of the same age is a '동갑'. So a '동급생' can be a different age. People in different grades are called '선배' and '후배'.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아빠를 설득해서 강아지를 키우기로 했어요.
examples.en: Mom persuaded Dad, and they decided to get a puppy.
I tried to persuade my friend, but it was no use.
Isn't there a good way to persuade the team leader?

examples.ko: 그를 설득하려고 몇 시간 동안 이야기했어요.
examples.en: I talked for hours to persuade him.

examples.ko: 발표에서 청중을 설득하는 것이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: Persuading the audience is the most important thing in a presentation.

examples.ko: 제가 설득하면 아마 같이 갈 거예요.
examples.en: If I persuade her, she'll probably come along.

explain: '강요하다'는 억지로 시키는 것이고, '설득하다'는 이유를 들어 상대가 이해하게 하는 것이에요. 설득을 받은 쪽은 '설득되다'라고 해요. '-을/를 설득하다'로 써요.
explain_en: '강요하다' is forcing someone, whereas '설득하다' is giving reasons so they understand. The person who ends up convinced is described with '설득되다'. The pattern is '-을/를 설득하다'.

examples.en: I talk over my career path with my parents.
I discussed the travel plans with my friend.

examples.ko: 어려운 일은 혼자 하지 말고 의논하세요.
examples.en: Don't handle difficult things alone; talk them over.
I'll decide after we talk it over as a family.
We need time to discuss it with the team members.
I came because I have something to talk over with you, teacher.

explain: '의논하다'는 같이 정할 일을 이야기할 때 써요. '상의하다'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 병원이나 상담소처럼 전문가에게 고민을 말할 때는 '상담하다'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: Use '의논하다' for talking something through to decide it together. '상의하다' is used almost the same way. When you bring a worry to an expert, like at a clinic or counseling center, '상담하다' fits better.

examples.ko: 아침 아홉 시에 학교 앞에 집합해요.
examples.en: We assemble in front of the school at nine in the morning.
The students assembled on the field.
We will meet up in front of the station tomorrow.
The place to assemble is in front of the main gate.
After everyone gathered, we left together.
We gathered on time and boarded the bus.

explain: 집합하다는 정해진 시간에 정해진 장소로 모이는 일에 써서 선생님이나 팀장이 지시하는 느낌이 있어요. 친구끼리 약속할 때는 '모이다', '만나다'를 써요. '집합!'은 모이라는 구령으로도 쓰여요.
explain_en: 집합하다 is for gathering at a set time and place, and it feels like an instruction from a teacher or team leader. Friends making plans use '모이다' or '만나다'. '집합!' is also used as an order to gather.
